sun-yellow.$description: Sun Yellow — Primary action buttons, card highlights, decorative shapes, the signature pop — the only color with true filled-button authority

hot-pink.$description: Hot Pink — Decorative borders, accent shapes, image overlays — used as visual punctuation, never as fill

lime-burst.$description: Lime Burst — Decorative strokes, border accents, secondary highlight — energetic counterweight to Sun Yellow

periwinkle.$description: Periwinkle — Card background, secondary action — the cool blue in an otherwise warm palette

spring-green.$description: Spring Green — Card backgrounds, nav highlights — warmer, more muted companion to Lime Burst

bubblegum.$description: Bubblegum — Soft pink accent for secondary nav elements and tag pills

warm-linen.$description: Warm Linen — Primary page canvas, soft shadow color, border tint — the warm cream that holds the whole system together

paper-white.$description: Paper White — Card surfaces, elevated content blocks — barely warmer than pure white, just enough to feel like paper

pure-white.$description: Pure White — Hairline borders, dividers, input outlines, and card edges on light surfaces. Do not promote it to the primary CTA color

charcoal.$description: Charcoal — Dark hero section background, high-contrast text container — not pure black, a warmer near-black

stone.$description: Stone — Muted card backgrounds, secondary surfaces, neutral button fills

sand.$description: Sand — Warm neutral for soft fills, secondary card backgrounds

ink.$description: Ink — Primary text, hairline borders, icon strokes, logo — the structural color, used at extreme scale

fog.$description: Fog — Muted borders, secondary dividers, disabled states

ease-standard.$description: Body, nav, labels, captions, button text — the workhorse at a single 400 weight with tight negative tracking

ease-display.$description: Display headlines, hero text, section titles, decorative logo — runs at 400 weight only, so display impact comes from extreme scale (up to 100px) and tight tracking, never from bolding
